speaker: Doctor
text: Good morning, I am Dr. Agent. I see you have a history of a painful, swollen left ankle that resolved on its own, and now you are presenting with increasing pain and swelling in your right knee along with episodes of painful urination. Can you tell me how long these current knee symptoms have been lasting and how severe the pain is on a scale of 1 to 10?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient has been experiencing increasing pain and swelling in his right knee for the past 12 days. He reports pain with urination for the past 3 weeks and had a swollen, painful left ankle joint that resolved on its own about a week ago. He mentions being sexually active with 2 female partners and using condoms inconsistently. He also reveals that his mother has rheumatoid arthritis. The patient appears anxious.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Reactive Arthritis (Reiter's Syndrome) secondary to an untreated urinary tract infection.

The history of asymmetric oligoarthritis affecting the ankle and now the knee, combined with dysuria and high-risk sexual behavior in a young male, is highly suggestive of reactive arthritis. I will request a Urinalysis, Urine Culture, and HLA-B27 testing to confirm the diagnosis and rule out other causes like gonococcal arthritis.
